instruction: Give a 1-star rating to all songs in my Spotify song library which I have not liked. If I have already rated it higher, decrease it to 1.
notes: The library contents are unknown up front, so the problem uses representative songs: one unliked library song with no review by the supervisor (needs spotify.review_song with rating 1), one unliked library song the supervisor already rated higher (needs spotify.update_song_review to rating 1), and one liked library song that must be left untouched (review actions require (not (liked ?s)), so it can never be rated). show_song_library and show_liked_songs are single (paginated) calls whose results are modeled by the global knowledge predicates (library-listed)/(liked-listed) combined with the static facts (in-library ?s)/(liked ?s); per-song show_song_reviews (filtered by the supervisor's email, which comes from supervisor.show_profile and is also the Spotify username, hence email is a subtype of username) yields (reviews-checked ?s) which exposes the existing review id. Static (unreviewed ?s)/(has-review ?s ?r) decide which rating API applies. Because the goal is a set of per-song facts and quantified goals are disallowed, supervisor-complete-task takes the two to-be-rated songs as non-API record parameters and requires both distinct unliked library songs to be rated-one; it is the only action that asserts (task-completed), and every other action requires (not (task-completed)). In the real run the loop over show_song_reviews + review_song/update_song_review is repeated for every unliked library song; the rating value 1 is encoded as the object rating-1.
